chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorced his wife, or she redeemed herself (kharaj), or he separated from her (bara'a), is it permissible for him to marry her sister? He said: If he freed her bond of marriage and he did not have a right of return over her, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister.
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about a man whose wife redeemed herself from him, is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before her waiting period expires? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and he does not have a right of return, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his ex-wife's sister after a final divorce?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the conditions under which a man may marry his ex-wife's sister, emphasizing that the key criterion is the severance of the marital bond (ibra') and the absence of the right of return (raj'a), rather than the mere passage of time. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the finality of the divorce and the procedural requirements for proposing to the sister, ensuring no conflict of interest or prohibition exists during the iddah period.
